output_token_limit_justification.rationale: The limit is derived from the largest file the baseline strategy must re-emit, plus an allowance for provider-side reasoning, so a truncation reflects the task, not the strategy. It is identical for all three strategies and is recorded per attempt.

retry_policy: bounded; transient HTTP 429 only; HTTP 402 and daily/per-minute quota caps are never retried

enforced: environment scrubbed to PATH/TMPDIR/LANG/PYTHON* (no provider credential)
PYTHONPATH restricted to the evaluation directory, user site-packages disabled
macOS Seatbelt profile: no network, no access to the operator's home/project directory (the .env credential is unreadable)
POSIX resource limits: RLIMIT_CPU, RLIMIT_AS, RLIMIT_NPROC, RLIMIT_FSIZE
not_enforced: no file-system confinement beyond the rules above

seed_policy: request-level seed per cell, derived from request_seed_base and the cell's position in the deterministic schedule

provenance.description: Reduced 100-request schedule for the modular task family. Every task is attempted with every method at least once (60 cells); the remaining 40 cells give each task exactly 5 attempts in total and split the budget 34/33/33 across the three methods. This is NOT 20 tasks x 5 repetitions x 3 methods: that design needs 300 requests.

notes: This benchmark evaluates three editing strategies of this project on synthetic HumanEval-derived repair tasks. It is not the HumanEval benchmark and produces no HumanEval pass rate.
Mock-mode runs are pipeline tests only and are not measurements.
The evaluation sandbox is best-effort isolation, not a security boundary: filesystem and subprocess containment are absent and the socket guard can be bypassed by a child process.
